[spoiler=war post 2][b][u]Arenenge breaks the jammers and secures the skys.[/u][/b]

It seems the Techno(k)ratic people have failed to complete their adjective. The adjective being to render the Arenese communication completely by using scrambling devices. Their choice of their device lead to their downfall. Unfortunately, the land jamming systems had worked on some scouting planes, but the pilots quickly understood what was going on and communicated before anything major happened. Also unfortunately, the land-to-air missiles had targeted and destroyed three of the six planes: two UAVs and one manned plane. The fleet moved slightly, about 20 miles further from the coast to avoid (if any) costal batteries from hitting them. At the same time, the scouting planes had picked up a small fleet of unidentified flying objects. The cruisers immediately sent an order to send out UAVs that would skim the water and look for traces of anything. If they found an object, they would lock on to a cluttered group of them and ram into that group, taking them out. For further protection, a second set of UAVs that had an attached EMP device onto them would fry any number of aircraft that is in its proximity. These two 'rows' of UAVs formed the outer ring, which sat about 70-80 miles from the ships. This ring was used as the detector ring. It's really hard to see a drone if it looks and acts like an airplane. But the way the Arenese would go around it, is that some radars of the UAVs would have a lower or higher sensitivity than others. If it looks like a plane on one, but a drone on another, it's probably a drone. When a drone passes this ring, the belly-mounted sensors will take an image of it, enhance it via AI, and send it to the pilot's targeting system.

The middle layer ring was composed of suicide drones, which were stupidly fast and explosive. On impact or controlled detonation from its AI, these drones would send large fragments all around and hit anything within fifty meters. Bobian F-15EX Fighter jets are shot into the middle ring as a backup if Arenenge's ship-to-air fragmentation missiles don't already hit them. The F-15EX fighter jets are equipped with multiple air-to-air missiles, and extra smoke flares. The smoke is really hot, so it blends in with the jet. This confuses the drone's ai targeting system, and makes it fall into the water before the jete ever needs to use a missile or gun. The Bobian Airforce learned from their past mistakes and simply attached anti-drone weaponry to it, to make it that much better.

The inner ring was made up of most of the Jets on the carriers, which were the F-35C fighter jet, the A-18C basic fighting jet, and some F-16C fighter jets. The F35C was the prize of the Arenese fleet. Capable of blending in with friendly drones, and tricking enemy radar to sneak onto their planes and shoot them down without them even knowing. The A-18C and f-16C were the backbone of this operation. They were cheaper and Used to scare the enemy planes. Their air-to-air missiles were more advanced than the plane itself, which could seek using IR vision if it detected itself was getting jammed. Though it looks expensive, Arenenge could use this all they wanted without cost deficiency. The fleet itself was also in the Inner ring. The cruisers had deployed the drones but weren't just there for the drones. They were fitted with seven SM-2 missile launchers. Each of these missiles can hit from over 90 miles, which means this is a big worry for planes even outside of all three rings. This missile could go up to Mach 3, and hit planes at 80,000 feet in the air. Remember that there are about four cruisers, not including Bobian ones, that can hold these. If only I could put stealth o these missiles, sigh. Unfortunately, I have to make this realistic. So, I have to reduce the number of SAMs to just one, and the amount of missiles to just 21. But that's where the destroyers come in. Since I can't fit any torpedoes on the cruisers, I will just have to fit them on the destroyers. A typical destroyer can carry 21 torpedoes. They can launch three from one side. They have two sides doubling three to six. I have about six destroyers in Squadron A. Three are defensive, and three are regular. This totals the defensive torpedoes to 42 defensive torpedoes, and 42 regular ones, making 82 total. The defensive destroyer torpedoes are the Russian Sirena, and Türkiye's ZOKA. The Sirena is a torpedo that uses acoustic sounds to mimic a submarine. To make it even more convincing, they travel at the same speed. The ZOKA emits submarine like signatures to lure the enemy torpedoes away. If all of this fails, then an offensive torpedo will hit the enemy torpedo and destroy it. The offensive torpedoes include but not limited to: the MU90 Impact lightweight torpedo, and the Mk 54 Lightweight Torpedo. Both of which don't require over horizon sonar and rely on their own target discrimination system. Both have the total annihilation radius of 10+ meters, and heavy injury radius of 30+ km. These torpedoes are ideal for dealing with threats relatively fast, as they both have a speed of over 40 knots.[/spoiler]

[spoiler= Children of the North Sea (Expansion Post)] To the east of the Jomslandic mainland, where the wind sings over flat pastures and the sea battles the shore with relentless patience, lies the proud and quiet nation of Frjósland. A land of salt and silt, of windmills and watchful levees, it had stood independent from the commonwealth for over two centuries. Yet the bonds between Frjósland and Jomsland had never truly broken. Their people, shaped by wind, sea, and a stubborn will to survive, shared more than their Teutonic blood and seafaring skills.
Frjósland, whose name means Land of the Shepherds, had once been a jewel in the diadem of the First Commonwealth. As far back as the 9th century, it was Frjósian builders, masters of coastal protection, who built the first dikes along Jomslands eastern coast. These early structures, crude by todays standards, laid the foundation for the safety of thousands. Without them, much of the coastal territory would have been devoured by the storm tides ages ago. The Frjósians had brought with them the ancient knowledge of Siel Gates, complex sluice gates that allowed rainwater and river runoff to drain into the sea during low tide while shutting fast at high tide to prevent the deadly backflow of storm surges. The system of Binnendeiche (inner dikes), Außendeiche (outer dikes), and Sielanlagen ensured that the low marshlands remained arable. Every citizen of Frjósland was born with a spade in their hands. The Gods made the world, the Frjósians liked to say, but we made Frjósland.
Over the centuries, the tides of politics had driven Frjósland away from its Jomslandic kinsmen. During the Gorms Flood in the year 1812 and the collapse of the First Commonwealth, Frjósland declared autonomy and adopted a chieftain-led Tingbund, a confederation of marshland elders who governed by vote. Though independent, the Frjósians never forgot their roots. Every year, at the Drachenfest, they reenacted the arrival of their ancestors in Jomsland, wearing seal-leather boots and carrying White Dragon Banners.
By the year 2025, Frjóslands future felt increasingly uncertain. Rising sea levels threatened its coastal defenses. The pan-continental war with the THEP loomed ever closer. Frjóslands neutrality no longer seemed noble but dangerously naive. That was when Prince Ubbe, heir of High King Jorik III, crossed the Teutonic Bay.
It was early summer when Ubbe travelled to Frjósland by ship, passing the breakwaters of Gróthavn, Frjóslands largest and oldest port city. The name meant "great harbor," and true to its name, it bustled with grain ships, long trawlers, and seaweed-laden barges. Gróthavn had been a vital trade hub in the old days of the First Commonwealth. Now, it served as the stage for one of the most symbolic reunifications in modern Elseyr. The prince came not as a conqueror, but as a shieldbrother.
He wore no crown, only a weathered wolfskin cloak and the silver amulet of his house. In public speeches across the city square and inside the Hóltshús, the Hall of the Chieftains, he spoke of shared history, shared struggle, and shared fate. He recalled how Frjósians once taught the Jomslanders to master the sea and how both now faced a greater storm. Inside the Hall, Frjóslands ruling assembly met with Ubbe behind closed doors. For three days and nights, they negotiated terms. The prince promised Frjósland local autonomy, cultural protection, and joint coastal protection funding. In exchange, Frjósland would swear allegiance to the Second Commonwealth, send representatives to the Allthing in Heiðabýr, and contribute help to the war effort.
On the fourth day, the decision came. The chieftains, by unanimous vote, agreed to rejoin the Second Commonwealth. On the steps of the Hólrshús, before thousands of cheering bystanders, Ubbe was declared Jarl of Frjósland. He took the oath with one hand on the Spadesword of Elfgroet, an ancient Frjósian artifact said to be forged from the iron of a sunken longship, and the other hand in the water of the great canal of Grothavn.
The next week, a Frjósian Legion of 50,000, made up of veterans of coastal defense forces, militias, and voluntary regiments, was created. Trained in amphibious warfare, coastal defense, and sabotage in muddy terrain, they were integrated into the command structure of the Jomslandic Sea Battalion.
As the Frjósian Legion rejoined the Jomslandic forces, so too did the Frjósian expertise in coastal protection. Frjósian dike-builders were dispatched to inspect the dikes in eastern Jomsland. Older flood maps were digitized and integrated into the military logistics network. Even the Siel Gates were modernized with hydraulic steel systems, preserving their original function while allowing for remote operation.
Thus did Frjósland, once more, find its place within the arms of the Commonwealth.[/spoiler]

[quote=western_view;60007115][spoiler=Lost at Sea][b][i]Western View Paper[/i][/b]
Earlier today radio stations in North Western View, as well as ships in the Nestor ocean, picked up a mysterious message from a ship, the message was an SOS, but it also had a lot of static as well as what sounded like a fire alarm, and rushing water. Rescue teams were sent to the area, but they only found a single sheet of paper, with the faded words Leviathan. Operators soon realized that the SS Leviathan was the only ship unaccounted for. The SS Leviathan was a Leviathan class oil tanker, carrying 2 million tons of oil, headed for Eastornia-Kolionia. Many speculate that the ship was attacked, seeing that it's route led it close to a country in active war, though many say it is unlikely for SS Leviathan to be attacked, after all it was flying the Western View flag, and wasn't in an active war zone, and the Leviathan's coordinates suggest it was hit by a large storm, but since there have been no survivors found yet, we can only go by the single radio message the Leviathan sent.

Other facts about the SS Leviathan.
[list][*]The SS Leviathan is the largest Wessern ship ever built, at almost 1,000ft long.
[*]The SS Leviathan could carry up to 3 million tons of oil.
[*]The SS Leviathan entered service around 2 years ago, and it builders 4 years to build
[*]The SS Leviathan housed 40 crew memebers
[*]The SS Leviathan could go 17 knots in clear weather
[*]The SS Leviathan was considered to most advanced Wessern ship
[*]The SS Leviathan was built and launched in Wessernia, Western View's capital[/spoiler]
[nation]Eastornia-Kolionia[/nation][/quote]
[spoiler=Search, Rescue, and Ivestigate][b][i]Wetsern View Paper[/i][/b]
After a few weeks of searching, rescue teams finally found something. An inflatable life raft, with a tarp over it, inside they found two people. They were both rushed to the hospital, both had been exposed to the elements for way to long. Luckily they're currently in stable condition, mostly due to Western View's amazing doctors. The two people have been confirmed to be from the SS Leviathan, and have been fully identified. They are two of the ships bridge crew, Antonio Gasduiy (gasd-oo-E), and Joe Hangradais (Hangr-a-dias). Currently investigators from the WVTSB (Western View Transportation Safety Bureau) have been waiting for Antonia and Joe to be released from the hospital. While they wait, the WVTSB investigates the little clues they have. they have determined that the paper came from the ships files, and that the ship was not attacked by another country, because the SS Leviathan was fitted with sirens incase there was an external attack, but that doesn't rule out a bomb or a terrorist attack. The WVTSB has been searching for the wreck of the lost ship, with the militaries help, of course. Head council member Tony Messiaon has come yesterday with a speech about the lost ship, which has been getting a lot of attention, in his speech he stated, "This is a sad day for many, there are still 38 missing, I know, but we must keep moving forward, we must keep helping this country survive, and to thrive, even in the utmost of circumstances, but we are allowed to feel sad, or angry, we should feel sad and angry, in fact let us have a minute of silence for those missing right now." As the country of Western View grieves the missing, the search for any clues, survivors, or the wreck are in full swing, a quarter of the Wessernian navy and air force is involved in the search, and people are on the beaches searching for wreckage. After his speech Tony Messiaon has asked for an "Entire search, I do not think [nation]Technokratisches Kaiserreich[/nation] will help, but I will ask anyway, all countries that border the Nestor Ocean, please search your beaches for any pieces of metal, if you do find any, and are unable to identify it, please send it to us, and if you do identify it as the SS Leviathan's please send it to us immediately." There have been reports of oil in the ocean, so volunteers are coming to help save the dolphins, and other species from the growing crisis.[/spoiler]
